observed_change: 81% of institutional sales and service teams use AI to generate and refine RFP content; top uses are automating responses (80%), searching content libraries (53%) and suggesting DDQ answers (53%).
scenario_not_observed: Fully automated submission without human review.
needs_human_supervision: Checking every answer against approved, current, compliant content; hallucinated answers are the top-cited barrier (vendor survey).
uncertain: How fast review time falls; whether clients start issuing more or longer RFPs in response.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) Juniors may draft less from scratch and spend more time verifying and maintaining the content library; the skill shifts from writing to judgement about accuracy.

observed_change: 77% use AI for note-taking and summarising meetings with clients, prospects and consultants.
scenario_not_observed: AI attending and following up on meetings unaided.
needs_human_supervision: Deciding what was actually agreed, what is sensitive and who must act.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) A traditional junior task that taught listening is partly automated; the learning must come from attending and being questioned on the meeting instead.

observed_change: 63% of managers in one study automate repetitive workflows such as daily report generation; 85% of UK fiduciary managers use AI mainly for drafting reports and emails.
scenario_not_observed: Client-ready performance explanation with no human sign-off.
needs_human_supervision: Numbers reconciliation, attribution accuracy and tone when performance is poor.
uncertain: Regulators' expectations on accountability for AI-drafted client communications.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) Less time building packs; more responsibility for checking them.
evidence_note: Supported inference (Clearwater via press); Verified (Isio via Pensions Age)

observed_change: Lower adoption: 32% draft prospecting letters, 26% identify prospects, 26% plan sales strategy with AI.
scenario_not_observed: AI-led prioritisation of which clients to pursue.
needs_human_supervision: Relationship context, suitability and whether to pursue at all.
uncertain: Whether adoption stays low or is simply earlier in the curve.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) Client research remains a junior task for now, with better tools.

observed_change: 55% of managers have AI in at least one investment process; only 5% give it autonomous or semi-autonomous authority.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) Not a client-coverage task; relevant because client teams must explain how AI is used.

observed_change: BCG estimates AI could cut asset-manager costs 25-35% over three to five years (estimate). Reported 2026 cuts at BlackRock, BNP Paribas AM and Morgan Stanley cite efficiency and integration.
scenario_not_observed: Large reductions in junior client-facing hiring caused by AI.
uncertain: No credible data retrieved linking AI to entry-level distribution hiring.
effect_on_junior_learning: (Layer B) If preparation work shrinks, firms may hire fewer juniors or expect earlier client exposure; either is a scenario.
evidence_note: Verified (BCG estimate exists); Not publicly established (junior hiring effect)
